course.title: How Machine Learning Works
course.tagline: Work out by hand and then in code how a model learns from labelled examples, test it honestly on held-out data, set its threshold from error costs, catch leaks and write down its limits
course.description: Participants work out how supervised learning turns labelled examples into predictions, by hand first and then in code. They fit a nearest-neighbour rule and a linear model on paper, make a model overfit on purpose, choose a decision threshold from error costs and base rates, and hunt leaks seeded in a pipeline. Labs run on a laptop with small public or synthetic tabular data, and the capstone is an honest modelling report with a model card, defended in person.
course.audience: Beginners. Graduates, career changers and computing professionals preparing for Developer or Specialist courses, who can run a Python notebook but have not yet studied AI methods.
prerequisites: FND-PRG-101 Python Programming for Data and AI
Writes short Python functions and loops; a passed placement exercise is accepted instead of FND-PRG-101
Uses school algebra; the derivative of a squared error is taught in the pre-work
course.format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

outcomes.text: Explain how a supervised learner fits a prediction rule by minimising a loss, given a ten-row table and a one-feature linear model
outcomes.evidence: a hand-worked loss and two gradient steps, with a three-sentence explanation

outcomes.text: Distinguish training, validation and test data, and identify overfitting and underfitting from plotted curves, given six complexity and learning curves
outcomes.evidence: a diagnosis and remedy per curve, at least five of six correct

outcomes.text: Identify target, duplicate, preprocessing and temporal leakage in modelling pipelines, given eight short pipeline descriptions
outcomes.evidence: each leak named with its fix, at least six of eight correct

outcomes.text: Implement a train, validate and test workflow comparing a baseline, a linear model and a decision tree, given a tabular dataset and a starter notebook
outcomes.evidence: a notebook that runs end to end with a fixed seed and reports held-out metrics

outcomes.text: Compute confusion-matrix metrics and choose a threshold from error costs and the base rate, given test-set scores and a cost per error type
outcomes.evidence: a metrics table and a justified threshold

outcomes.text: Draft a one-page model card with intended use, data, metrics by subgroup and known limits, given the participant's capstone model
outcomes.evidence: a model card reviewed in the defence

case_study.name: Hurbuth Home Care Company
case_study.summary: Hurbuth (حُربُث) is a fictional private provider of home nursing and physiotherapy for older people in an unnamed city with five sectors; it wants a six-month fall-risk screen that turns the nurse's home assessment into a flag for a physiotherapy home programme. Every file is synthetic and written with a fixed seed by labs/prepare_data.py: 4,776 assessments of 2,500 clients (codes only), a later batch from a newly opened sector, an export with three seeded leaks, and two further screens of the same company for the capstone and the follow-up task.

days.label: Capstone
days.title: Capstone: a modelling report and its defence
days.subtitle: Ten minutes each: six of talk, then four of questions in which the participant re-runs the notebook and explains a result the instructor selects

capstone.summary: A modelling report on a provided public or synthetic dataset, with a baseline, two models, a threshold decision and a model card, defended in ten minutes; the follow-up task repeats it on a second dataset
capstone.submission: Individual. A public GitHub repository link holding the modelling report notebook on the admission screen (labs/capstone/), run end to end with its fixed seed and its history kept: a baseline, two models, a threshold decision from the stated costs and base rate, and a one-page model card. Then a ten-minute defence: six minutes of talk and four of questions, in which the participant re-runs the notebook and explains a result the instructor selects.

rubric.criterion: Held-out workflow: a baseline and two models compared on validation with a fixed seed, the test set opened once, the notebook running end to end
Leakage-safe data handling: the split by date, the field recorded after the outcome removed, every preprocessing step fitted on training rows inside a pipeline
Threshold decision: chosen from the stated error costs and the base rate, with the confusion matrix and metrics at that threshold
Model card: intended use, data, metrics by subgroup with counts, known limits and who should not rely on the model, with an owner and a different reviewer
Defence: re-runs the notebook and explains the result the instructor selects
